coverageDimensions:
SERVICE coverage: this is the one dimension the page actually gives, and it gives it well. It means "for how many AWS services can CloudTrail record VPC-endpoint API calls as network activity events". Numerator 62 named services (or 76 eventSource principals if the map prefers configuration identifiers — pick one, never both). Denominator is not on the page: the count of AWS services must come from an external service list, so the ratio is only as good as that outside denominator. Sign is one-way — supported is stated, unsupported never is.

REGION coverage: the page gives NOTHING. It contains no Region list, no Region-availability table, no "available in all Regions where X is available" sentence, and no Region exclusions. The only Region strings on the page are the placeholder {{region}} in CLI commands and us-east-1 inside example ARNs, which are example data and must not be harvested. "MultiRegionEnabled": true in the JSON output is an event data store setting, not a Region availability claim. If the map needs Region coverage for this capability, it must come from another page.

RESOURCE TYPE coverage: the page gives essentially NOTHING positive. Network activity events are scoped by service and by VPC endpoint, not by resource type, so there is no resource-type axis to fill. The single resource-shaped statement on the page is negative: Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Points are not supported. Recording that as the whole of resource-type coverage would be misleading — the honest record is one stated exclusion under one service, with no positive resource-type enumeration anywhere.

Two further dimensions the page does state and which a service/Region/resource-type frame would lose: the destination dimension (trails and event data stores, with event data stores limited to type "CloudTrail events"), and the selector-field × destination matrix (userIdentity.arn on trails only). Both are capability matrices, not ratios.

features.featureName: Services for which you can log network activity events
features.reasoning: The coverage claim here is "CloudTrail network activity events reach AWS service Y". The values are AWS service names (AWS AppConfig, Amazon Athena, AWS KMS, Amazon S3 …), which are an external universe: those services exist whether or not CloudTrail chooses to log them, and the denominator (all AWS services) comes from outside this page. That makes a ratio meaningful. Counted by hand off the bullet list: 62 items, the Note under Amazon S3 excluded from the count because it is an exclusion, not a 63rd service.
features.scope: Configurable on both trails and event data stores; event data stores must be of type "CloudTrail events". Not logged by default — each event source must be configured explicitly.
features.statuses: 62 stated supported, 0 stated unsupported at service granularity. The list is positive-only prose bullets under "You can log network activity events for the following services" — there is no Yes/No column and no negative service. One sub-service exclusion is stated as a Note attached to the Amazon S3 bullet: "Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Points are not supported." Amazon S3 itself stays supported; only that feature is carved out. Every AWS service absent from the list is UNSTATED, not stated-unsupported — the page never says "all other services are not supported", so absence must be recorded as silence, not as a No.
features.waived: The same list, twice. This feature and 'eventSource valid values' enumerate one set of services: the prose names and the service principals of the same event sources. We read the principals, which are unambiguous, and publish one row. Two rows here would be one capability counted twice.

features.featureName: eventSource valid values for network activity events
features.reasoning: These are AWS service principal names (kms.amazonaws.com, s3.amazonaws.com, rolesanywhere.amazonaws.com …), an AWS-wide identifier space that exists independently of CloudTrail, so the axis is external and it is a service axis expressed in machine-readable form. It is NOT a second capability in the product sense — it is the same capability as the 62-service list, enumerated at a different granularity, and the two lists disagree. They must never be summed (138 is a fiction) and the map must pick one as canonical. The 76 exceeds the 62 for two reasons visible on the page: one service can have several event sources (Amazon WorkMail → workmail + workmailmessageflow; AWS Transform → transform + transform-agents + transform-custom; Amazon Transcribe → transcribe + transcribestreaming), and several event sources have no matching entry in the prose service list at all (aco-automation, bedrock-agentcore, cloudoptimization, comprehend, iot, nova-act, rolesanywhere, ssm, user-subscriptions, voiceid). The prose list is the safer human-facing coverage axis; this list is the safer configuration-checking axis.
features.scope: Value of the `eventSource` advanced event selector field; `Equals` operator only; one field selector required per event source.
features.statuses: 76 values, all stated as valid — this is a positive-only list with no negatives. The wording is "Valid values include", so treat it as possibly non-exhaustive rather than closed. No Yes/No column, no footnote, no retired or deprecated marking anywhere in it.

features.featureName: Advanced event selector fields for network activity events
features.reasoning: This is a genuine enumerable set with a stated exclusion and a stated second dimension, so it is coverage-shaped. But the axis is CloudTrail's own list of selector fields for its own event category — the service holds 100% of it by construction, so 6/6 is meaningless as a ratio and must be shown as a capability matrix (field × destination), never as a percentage. The same applies to `errorCode`: one value out of one is not 100% coverage of anything. Recording this at all is optional for a coverage map; if recorded, it must be flagged catalogue so no ratio is computed.
features.scope: Trails vs event data stores — the page states this second dimension explicitly for one field.
features.statuses: 6 fields: 2 required (`eventCategory`, `eventSource`) and 4 optional (`eventName`, `errorCode`, `vpcEndpointId`, `userIdentity.arn`). All 6 work on trails; 5 of 6 work on event data stores. The one stated negative is a plain prose sentence, not a table: "CloudTrail supports this field for trails only. You cannot filter network activity events on userIdentity.arn for event data stores." Within `errorCode` there is exactly 1 valid value, `VpceAccessDenied` ("Currently, the only valid errorCode is VpceAccessDenied").

shouldNotExtract: The **Contents** block and every **Topics** block — they are navigation, and their entries ("Example: Log VpceAccessDenied events for AWS KMS", "Logging network activity events with the AWS Command Line Interface") look exactly like capability names. The whole CLI and console section: put-event-selectors / get-event-selectors / create-event-data-store / update-event-data-store / get-event-data-store and the SDK operations PutEventSelectors, GetEventSelectors, CreateEventDataStore, UpdateEventDataStore, GetEventDataStore are API operations, not services and not coverage. The five services used in the examples (CloudTrail, EC2, KMS, Secrets Manager, S3) are an illustrative subset, never the supported list. The eventName illustrations CreateKey, ListKeys, CreateTrail, CreateEventDataStore are examples of an unbounded field, not an enumerated set. The quota "a maximum of 500 specified values for all conditions" is a quota. The pricing sentences and both AWS CloudTrail Pricing links are pricing. "Network activity events are not logged by default" is a default state, not non-coverage. Sample ARNs, account ids 111122223333 / 123456789012, region us-east-1, vpce-example8c1b6b9b7, RetentionPeriod 366 and the timestamps in the JSON outputs are example data. The console click-path steps ("Choose Edit", "Switch to advanced event selectors") are procedure. The trailing "See also" bullet about Skills for AI coding assistants and the Agent Toolkit CLI command is AWS boilerplate appended to every page.
trap: Fusing or summing the two lists. They are the same capability counted twice — 62 service names and 76 eventSource strings — and a careless parser either adds them (138), or reports 76 services (wrong: transcribe and transcribestreaming are one service, as are workmail/workmailmessageflow and transform/transform-agents/transform-custom), or reports 62 and silently drops the ten event sources that have no prose entry (aco-automation, cloudoptimization, nova-act, rolesanywhere, ssm, comprehend, iot, user-subscriptions, voiceid, bedrock-agentcore). The second trap is the Amazon S3 Note: it sits between the "Amazon S3" and "Amazon SageMaker AI" bullets at a deeper indent, so a line-based parser takes "Multi-Region Access Points" as a 63rd supported item when it is in fact the page's only service-side exclusion — an inversion of sign. Third: reading the CLI examples as the supported list and emitting 5 services. Fourth: treating errorCode's single value VpceAccessDenied as a finding-type catalogue and reporting 1/1 = 100%. Fifth: reading the 62-item list as closed-world and marking every unlisted AWS service as "not supported" — the page states no negative at service level, so absence is silence.
whatThePageStates: The page documents CloudTrail network activity events: CloudTrail records AWS API calls that reach a service through a VPC endpoint the customer owns, so the endpoint owner can see resource operations made from inside a private VPC (for example, credentials from outside the organization that try to use the endpoint). It enumerates two things that can be counted: the AWS services for which network activity events can be logged (a prose bullet list of 62 service names), and the valid `eventSource` values that an advanced event selector may specify (76 service-principal strings). It also enumerates the six advanced event selector fields available for this event category, and states where each one works. The rest is configuration procedure: console steps, AWS CLI examples, and SDK operation names.
